title: Warehouses were common along the train track. This warehouse and apartments were behind and attached to Ellis and Shaw
description: At 7:30 a.m. in 1912, a fire broke out in the Commercial Hotel after proprietor George MacCallum built a fire in the kitchen stove and returned to bed. He awoke to the smell of smoke. Located on the east side of the railway track, the building operated as both a hotel and a restaurant. The fire destroyed the CPR dining room on the first floor, ending the tradition of passengers dining in Hartland during train stops; the trade shifted to Woodstock. Although the building was not completely destroyed, the hotel business ended. It was later renovated, with the top floor converted to rental units and at street level adapted into warehouses with loading wharves on the railroad side to easily load farm produce into boxcars.
